findings.issue_text: When a refreshed token response omits refresh_token, the code overwrites it with the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" instead of preserving the existing refresh token, permanently destroying the real refresh token in the DB and breaking future refreshes

minimumTokenResponseSchema builds property keys using z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString(), which both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" instead of a dynamic key, so the schema only recognizes access_token and silently strips all other fields (expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, token_type) when credential-sync mode is enabled, corrupting stored credentials for Google, Office365, and Zoom

When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is used, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw unread fetch Response object, but callers (Google, Hubspot, Zoho-Bigin, ZohoCRM) expect different shapes (res.data wrapper, typed object, axios response), causing runtime TypeErrors when credential sync is enabled

zoho-bigin CalendarService.refreshAccessToken calls refreshOAuthTokens with a bare credentialId identifier instead of credential.userId like other integrations, resulting in either a ReferenceError or the wrong id being sent to the sync endpoint

Salesforce CalendarService fetches a refreshed token unconditionally on every connection build without checking whether the current access token is still valid, causing an unnecessary OAuth round-trip and DB write on every operation

Salesforce CalendarService checks response.statusText !== "OK" as a success check, which is unreliable since statusText can be empty or differently cased, causing false failures on successful refreshes; should check response.ok/response.status instead

The webhook secret in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts is compared using plain !== string comparison, which is not constant-time and is vulnerable to timing attacks against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
The find-then-create/update pattern for locating a credential by userId+appId in app-credential.ts is not atomic, allowing concurrent webhook calls to race and create duplicate credential rows
The app-credential.ts webhook handler does not check req.method, so non-POST requests are processed instead of returning 405

office365calendar CalendarService now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" error unconditionally on parse failure instead of logging via console.error and continuing, losing diagnostic detail and changing failure behavior from graceful degradation to an exception
zoho-bigin api/add.ts hardcodes redirectUri to the literal string "zoho-bigin" instead of deriving it from appConfig.slug, creating a maintenance hazard if the slug ever diverges from the literal

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema builds property keys using z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString(), which both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" instead of a dynamic key, so the schema only recognizes access_token and silently strips all other fields (expiry_date, refresh_token, scope, token_type) when credential-sync mode is enabled, corrupting stored credentials for Google, Office365, and Zoom

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: ..., [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names are evaluated immediately and become a single literal key string (e.g. "[object Object]" / "ZodString"), not a wildcard/dynamic key matcher. As a result, when credential-sync mode is enabled, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will not validate typical OAuth token responses (which have keys like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc.), because it will require that one literal computed key to be present with a number. This can cause refresh flows that call `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (e.g. Google Calendar and Office365 in the diff) to throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` at runtime. The finding’s core claim (schema is broken due to `.toString()` computed keys) is verifiable from the diff, though the exact failure mode is more likely a parse failure than “silently strips all other fields.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook secret in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts is compared using plain !== string comparison, which is not constant-time and is vulnerable to timing attacks against CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authentication check compares the provided secret header to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

A normal string comparison is not constant-time and can (in principle) leak information via timing differences when an attacker can make repeated requests and measure response time, whereas secret comparisons should use a constant-time primitive like `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after normalizing to `Buffer`s. This is a concrete issue introduced by the diff because this endpoint is newly added and relies on this comparison for authorization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The find-then-create/update pattern for locating a credential by userId+appId in app-credential.ts is not atomic, allowing concurrent webhook calls to race and create duplicate credential rows

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }})` and then conditionally calls `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. That is a classic non-atomic read-then-write sequence: two concurrent webhook requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “no row” and both execute `create`, resulting in duplicate credential rows (or a unique-constraint error if such a constraint exists, which is not shown/handled in this diff). The diff itself shows no transaction/locking/upsert on a unique key to prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The app-credential.ts webhook handler does not check req.method, so non-POST requests are processed instead of returning 405

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` Next.js API route, the `handler` function never checks `req.method`. As written, any HTTP method (GET/PUT/etc.) will flow through the same logic (credential-sharing enabled check, webhook secret check, then `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and DB writes). For non-POST requests, `req.body` will typically be empty/invalid, causing `zod.parse` to throw (likely resulting in a 500), and even for other methods with a body it would still process updates. A reasonable implementation should restrict to POST and return 405 for others, so the finding is a real issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" error unconditionally on parse failure instead of logging via console.error and continuing, losing diagnostic detail and changing failure behavior from graceful degradation to an exception

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code previously did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)`, and if parsing failed it `console.error(...)` but still continued (it merged only when `tokenResponse.success` and then proceeded to `prisma.credential.update`). The diff replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, and in the new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` it explicitly `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when `safeParse` fails. This removes the previous detailed logging and changes behavior from logging+continuing to throwing an exception on parse failure.
